title: fix(plugin-security)!: a delegate can neither capture nor evict a direct grant beyond its subtree
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing) — an edit that points a direct permission-set grant at another user is judged on both holders it touches, the user it takes the grant from and the user it gives the grant to, so a delegated administrator no longer moves a grant away from a holder outside its subtree, or from a holder it cannot read. Nothing is widened: no export, error code or status is added.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: updated here — `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx` (the "Subtree anchoring" rule) states it; no `skills/**` file teaches moving a direct grant (`skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` says a delegate writes a grant only "for that set and user", which stays true).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:委派管理员(adminScope)把一条已存的直接授权(`sys_user_permission_set`)改指向另一个用户时,委派门现在同时判断两端的持有人——被拿走授权的原持有人和得到授权的新持有人;任一端在委派子树之外、或调用者读不到,都拒绝。
- 为什么改:落实规则「a delegate can neither capture nor evict a direct grant beyond its subtree」(ADR-0090 D12 把直接授权限定在子树内),与同级的 `sys_user_position` 判断前像与新值的做法一致。属于安全加固,细节归 security#1 席。
- 风险与回滚:收窄(BREAKING,patch 级,不新增错误码或状态):委派管理员不能再把子树外或读不到的持有人的授权改指给别人;拒绝与新持有人在子树外时完全同一个答案(`403 DELEGATION_SCOPE_VIOLATION`)。租户级管理员照旧可改;组织管理员的权利本来就只有新建和删除、不含原地编辑,答案不变。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- 先看:① `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts` 的 `assertDirectGrantWrite`(`fromHolder` 一段与其在逐 scope 判断里的分支,风险 hunk)及新增的 `storedHolderJudged`;② `delegated-admin-own-name-set.posture.test.ts` 末尾新增的三形态 describe;③ `delegated-admin-gate.test.ts` 末尾新增的 describe。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/delegated-admin-gate.test.ts src/delegated-admin-own-name-set.posture.test.ts`,预期 `Test Files 2 passed (2)`、`Tests 311 passed (311)`。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

**Rule.** A delegate can neither capture nor evict a direct grant beyond its subtree. A delegated write on a direct permission-set grant is judged on every holder it touches: an update that points a stored grant at another user is judged on the holder it takes the grant from and on the holder it gives the grant to (ADR-0090 D12, which scopes direct set grants to "inside the subtree").

- `assertDirectGrantWrite` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts`): when an update changes the grant's holder, the stored holder is judged exactly as the holder the write names — through the caller's own read (`targetUserUnits`, the read #31556 added), inside the subtree only through one of its business units — with the same reason, class, sentence and details. Mirrors the sibling door, `assertAssignmentWrite`, whose docblock reads "Pre-image (update/delete) must also lie inside the subtree — a delegate can neither capture nor evict assignments beyond it." The stored holder is named in the refusal only when the caller's own read returned it at its stored value (ruling of record 6649064874, kept as written). A stored grant that names no holder is moved only by a tenant-level administrator, as an unanchored assignment is modified only by one.
- Unchanged: the allowlist check on the permission set; an update that keeps the holder (already judged on the stored holder); an insert and a removal; tenant-level and organization administrators.
- `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`: the "Subtree anchoring" rule names both holders of a moved direct grant.
- `.changeset/delegated-grant-move-judges-both-holders.md`: `patch`, `fix(plugin-security)!:`, a rule-level BREAKING paragraph whose "Who moves" reads "A delegate can no longer re-point a direct grant away from a holder outside its subtree, nor away from a holder it cannot read.", and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, spelled as in `.changeset/delegated-unreadable-user-outside-subtree.md`.

**Docblocks of record touched — quoted.** One sentence of `judgesTargetUserThroughCallerRead`'s docblock (`[ADR-0090 D12; ruling on #26059, Q3]`) gains the new holder; the rest of every docblock is kept as written.

> Before: "it holds for every target user the gate judges: the holder a direct-grant write names (an insert, an update pointing the grant at another user), the holder a stored grant keeps (a delete, an update that leaves `user_id` as stored), and the user the explain doors ask about"
>
> After: "it holds for every target user the gate judges: the holder a direct-grant write names (an insert, an update pointing the grant at another user), the holder a stored grant keeps (a delete, an update that leaves `user_id` as stored), the holder an update pointing the grant at another user takes it from, and the user the explain doors ask about"

Untouched and still governing the new branch: the inline `[ADR-0090 D12; ruling on #26059, Q3]` comment ("the refusal is one reason, one class, one sentence and one set of details for all of them") and `[ruling of record 6649064874] Named only when the caller wrote or reads it`.

**Ruling #26059 Q3, the scope-violation class** (ruling of record 6416233738, item 3, verbatim):

> 3. server p2 — item 3, server half: the delegated-admin gate (`delegated-admin-gate.ts:403–503`, reasons `:1136–1179`) answers its own code (e.g. `DELEGATION_SCOPE_VIOLATION`, status 403, ADR-0112 ledger row), distinct from `PERMISSION_DENIED`.

A holder outside the subtree at the end the update takes the grant from is a target user outside the subtree, so it answers that class; a stored grant that names no holder is not the caller's own scope and keeps `PERMISSION_DENIED`.

## Tests

Named by the rule, on both rigs:

- `delegated-admin-gate.test.ts` (fake engine), new top-level describe "a delegate can neither capture nor evict a direct grant beyond its subtree: an update that points a stored grant at another user is judged on both holders" — 8 pins: a move FROM a holder outside TO one inside is refused for each of the four target states (no user, no membership, a unit outside, a unit inside the caller cannot read) with one answer; FROM an unreadable in-subtree holder is refused; TO a holder outside is refused, as before; the refusal is identical whichever end is outside (class, code, status, message, details and the REST envelope); CONTROL: a move between two readable in-subtree holders is admitted at either end; both holders are asked of the caller's own read under the write's own context; a holderless stored grant is moved only by a tenant admin; CONTROL: a tenant-level administrator moves the grant whichever end is outside and asks the read nothing.
- `delegated-admin-own-name-set.posture.test.ts` (real `ObjectQL` + SQL driver + `SecurityPlugin`), new describe "… — three postures", 7 pins in each of `single`, `group`, `isolated` (21): a delegate that administers direct grants is refused a move FROM a holder outside for each of the four states with one answer, at the gate and through the write door, and the grant stays; FROM an unreadable in-subtree holder, through the write door; TO a holder outside, as before; the same answer whichever end; CONTROL: a move between two readable in-subtree holders lands at either end; a delegate that cannot read the stored grant gets the same refusal without the stored holder's name (ruling of record 6649064874); CONTROL: a tenant-level administrator still moves the grant through the write door, and an organization administrator gets the answer it always got (its right creates and removes a grant, never edits one in place).

**Ablation** (one behaviour, committed first, `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with a trap restore): the new stored-holder judgment switched off on disk (anchor 1 → 0, blob `b8bd47cc` → `6f61fee6`) → `Tests 17 failed | 294 passed (311)`, the 17 red being exactly new pins of this rule — on the fake engine the FROM-end, unreadable-holder, identity, both-holders-read and holderless pins (5); on the posture rig the FROM-end, unreadable-holder, identity and unnamed-holder pins in each posture (4 × 3); every CONTROL and every TO-end pin stayed green. Restored: blob == HEAD (`b8bd47cc`), `git diff HEAD` empty. The subject is reached by relative imports from `src/` (no `dist/` on the path), so no rebuild sits between mutation and run.

## Acceptance notes

- **Organization administrator control.** The order asked that a tenant-level administrator and an organization administrator can still re-point the grant. Measured on the current `origin/main`: an organization administrator's right under ADR-0090 D12 (as amended 2026-10-17) creates and removes a grant and never edits one in place, so its update is refused before and after this change (`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, "'update' is not part of the right"). The pin holds it unchanged; the tenant-level administrator re-points as before.
- **Identity across ends.** The answer is identical whichever end is outside when the caller reads the stored grant. A caller that cannot read it is not told the stored holder's id (ruling of record 6649064874): class, code, status and details still match the other end; the sentence uses the unnamed form, as the keep-holder edit already does.
- **Holderless stored grant.** `user_id` is required on `sys_user_permission_set`, so no write door stores one; the branch fails closed for a row a system write left so.
- **Concurrent work on `plugin-security`.** #31443 (the organization-boundary helper in `delegated-admin-gate.ts`) landed on `main` while this branch was in flight; this branch merges it (`c1975e1faf`) cleanly, and every reading below is taken after that merge. The one open PR still touching `plugin-security`, #31588, edits only `people-org-assignment-nav-contribution.test.ts`.
